title: Participate in the implementation and evaluation of a safety and health management programme in the workplace

lessons.title: What a safety and health management programme needs
lessons.html:
A plan to keep people safe

A safety and health management programme is the workplace's organised plan to prevent injuries and illness. On a farm it covers tractors and machinery, chemicals, animals, workshops, packhouses, heat, fire and more. Under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, the employer must provide and maintain a safe workplace, and employees must take care of their own and others' safety and follow the rules.

Main parts of the programme

  • Policy and commitment: a signed safety policy showing that management takes safety seriously.
  • Responsibilities: who does what, for example the manager, supervisors, health and safety representatives, first aiders and fire team.
  • Hazard identification and risk assessment: listing hazards in each job and deciding how to control them.
  • Safe work procedures: written steps for risky jobs such as spraying, chainsaw work or working at height.
  • Training: induction for new workers and job-specific training.
  • PPE: the right equipment, issued, used and replaced.
  • Inspections: regular checks of work areas and equipment.
  • Incident reporting and investigation.
  • Emergency plans: fire, first aid, chemical spills, evacuation.
  • Records and review.

Health and safety representatives and committees

Workplaces with more than a certain number of employees must have health and safety representatives elected or appointed from workers, and a health and safety committee. Representatives inspect the workplace, take part in investigations and bring workers' concerns to management. Your workplace will tell you who your representative is.

Your role

  • Attend safety talks and training.
  • Follow procedures and use your PPE.
  • Report hazards, injuries and near misses.
  • Take part in inspections and risk assessments when asked.
  • Speak up: you know your job's dangers best.

lessons.title: Taking part in safety evaluations
lessons.html:
How safety performance is checked

A programme only works if someone checks it. The programme sets out how and when safety is evaluated. You may be asked to help.

Workplace inspections

Inspections use a checklist for each area. For example, a workshop checklist may ask:

  • Are guards fitted on the grinder and drill press?
  • Is the fire extinguisher in place, sealed and in date?
  • Are walkways clear and floors free of oil?
  • Are electrical cords undamaged?
  • Is the first aid box stocked?

When you take part:

  1. Get the correct checklist and understand each item.
  2. Walk the whole area. Look, listen and ask workers.
  3. Tick yes or no honestly, and write details of problems: what, where, how serious.
  4. Do not fix dangerous problems yourself unless you are trained; report them.
  5. Hand in the checklist and tell the supervisor of urgent dangers at once.

Other evaluation methods

  • Task observations: watching a job being done to see if the safe procedure is followed.
  • Incident investigations: finding why an accident or near miss happened.
  • PPE checks: is it being used, and is it in good condition?
  • Emergency drills: fire or evacuation drills, timed and reviewed.
  • Talking to workers: asking about hazards they face.

Reporting incidents

Report every injury, near miss and dangerous occurrence on the farm's form, the same day. Include date, time, place, people involved, what happened, and any injuries. Serious incidents must be reported to the Department of Employment and Labour as the law requires; your employer handles that. Never cover up an incident. Hidden incidents happen again.

lessons.title: Evaluating results and improving
lessons.html:
Looking at the results

After inspections and other checks, the results are compared with the programme's targets and standards. This shows what is working and what is not.

Simple measures of safety performance

MeasureExample
Inspections done on time10 of 12 monthly inspections completed
Problems found and fixed18 found, 15 fixed within the agreed time
Incidents and near missesNumber this month compared with last year
Training completedAll sprayer operators trained this season
PPE compliancePercentage of workers seen wearing the right PPE

A rise in near-miss reports can be a good sign: people are reporting more. Fewer injuries is the goal, but fewer reports may just mean people stopped reporting.

From findings to action

  1. List each problem found.
  2. Decide the action to fix it, for example "replace the missing grinder guard".
  3. Name the person responsible.
  4. Set a date.
  5. Check that it was done and that it worked.

This is often kept as an action list and discussed at the health and safety committee meeting.

Example from a farm

Inspections in the packhouse showed that forklift drivers often drove through the pedestrian walkway. The committee painted clear walkways, added a mirror at a blind corner and gave drivers a refresher talk. At the next inspection, observations showed the problem had nearly stopped.

Your contribution

  • Give honest information during evaluations.
  • Suggest practical improvements.
  • Follow up on actions in your area.
  • Help new workers learn the safe way.

Key points

  • A programme includes policy, responsibilities, risk assessment, procedures, training, PPE, inspections, incidents and emergencies.
  • Use checklists honestly and report dangers at once.
  • Report every injury and near miss the same day.
  • Turn findings into actions with a person and a date.
  • Check that actions were done and worked.

quiz.question: Which law requires the employer to provide and maintain a safe workplace?

options.text: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993

quiz.question: What does a health and safety representative do?

options.text: Inspects the workplace and brings workers' concerns to management

quiz.question: During an inspection you find a dangerous fault you are not trained to fix. What should you do?

options.text: Report it, and tell the supervisor at once if urgent

quiz.question: What must an action to fix a safety problem include?

options.text: The action, a responsible person and a date

quiz.question: Why can a rise in near-miss reports be a good sign?
An incident should be hidden if nobody was hurt.
